claim: this file was added by the slice but is outside slice A's Footprint. The Footprint at docs/plans/2026-10-27-e18-fix-round-1.md:42 names only result.schema.json, signoff.py, signoff_core/result.py, signoff_core/validate.py and tests/test_fr1_kept_notes.py.
scenario: requirements 4 and 5 were folded into the slice without widening the Footprint. A build-v2 footprint check against line 42 would flag this file, so the slice touched a path its spec does not authorize. test_fr1_kept_notes.py also imports `strict_skill_root` from it, so the authorized test depends on the unauthorized file.

claim: requirement 1 still says the note shape is "the same as `finding` except that `severity` is BLOCKER, MAJOR, MINOR or null". The built `$defs/note` (result.schema.json:1038) makes location, claim, scenario and evidence_kind string-or-null with no minLength or enum, and makes severity any string. That follows requirement 4 (line 31) and contradicts requirement 1 as written.
scenario: a reader grading against requirement 1 alone sees a note with `severity: "NOTE"` and `evidence_kind: "inferred"` accepted, which requirement 1 forbids.

claim: the schema's top-level description still says it carries the rule that a result with no raised findings has a non-empty `checks_executed`, "each entry with its output". This slice removed `output` from the check's `required` and allowed null.
scenario: a consumer trusting the description assumes every recorded check has a string `output`, then reads `null` or a missing key from a valid result.

claim: the verdict doc's method lines changed for every check, not only checks with null fields. A check whose output is an empty string used to render "→ " and now renders "→ no output". A null exit code used to render "exit None" and now renders "no exit code".
scenario: a tool or fixture that matches verdict-doc method lines byte for byte sees different text for an empty-output check. I did not run the full suite; `uv run ... -p 'test_*.py'` on the core suite would show whether any fixture depends on it.

claim: The pre-write stop now passes `**common` to `finish`, so the raised findings and the notes are in the stopped result. The comment at :855-858 says they "never make this stop's own result fail", but that only holds for the result schema. `finish` (signoff.py:197-198, :220-224) also runs `validate.semantic` on the stopped result. The proposal can also be refused by semantic rules that look at those same fields (`/findings` raised outside the source set, `/notes` outside-set note that is in the set). In that case the stop result fails the same rule again, and `finish` exits 4 (EXIT_VALIDATION) instead of 10. The old code dropped findings and notes from this stop, so it could not hit this.
scenario: `state.json`'s `source_set` and the adjudication's raised/notes partition differ. For example, a run dir edited between `record-answer` and `record`, or a future change to how `in_set` is computed at signoff.py:648-650 versus validate.py:103-105. `record` then refuses the proposal on `/findings`, writes the stopped result, and exits 4 with `semantic` errors. A caller reads that as the station's own validation failure, not a clean stop.

claim: The new schema check runs before the `settling` branch, so it also runs on a recovery pass where the receipt already exists. When it refuses there, the stop reports `writes_none: true` and `answer_refused: true`, even though the receipt may show project writes that already landed (log appends, block, card). The stop does not use `partial_from_receipt`, so the record says nothing was written when something was.
scenario: An old-version run (the live run's shape) lands the verdict doc, the records and the card, then dies or exits before it commits. Recovery `record` then runs under a schema that refuses the proposal. The result claims `writes_none` while the log holds this run's events. The semantic-only check had the same exposure before; this slice widens what can refuse there.

claim: the slice range also changes two files outside Slice B's Footprint (signoff.py, packet.py, test_fr1_provenance.py): this plan doc, and docs/records/docs__plans__2026-10-27-e18-fix-round-1.events.jsonl. The plan doc change is the Status line moving from "not started" to "built" plus new ledger subsections. The events file is excluded from the packet by `EXCLUDED_PREFIXES`.
scenario: a strict reading of "No other change" or "files changed outside its Footprint" flags these. They look like build-v2's own station records (commit d6a220e), not slice work, so this is probably expected bookkeeping. I raise it so the session can confirm the station is allowed to write them.

claim: `test_a_multibyte_character_across_the_cap_is_still_text` does not put the character across the old read boundary. It builds `padding(CAP-1) + "é"`, so both bytes of "é" sit at offsets CAP-1 and CAP. Both are inside the old CAP+1-byte read, so the old capped read decodes it fine.
scenario: the test passes on its equality assert, but it never exercises a UTF-8 sequence split at the CAP+1 read boundary. A regression that brings back a bounded read for the material in that one case would not be caught by this test as written. Probe result: The test's own input under the old capped read returns text of 524289 bytes, not None. An "é" starting at offset CAP returns None under the capped read and the correct text with `limit=None`.

claim: under the default cap, `read_text_or_none` decodes the first CAP+1 bytes with strict UTF-8. A file over 512 KiB that has a multibyte character straddling byte CAP+1 is therefore reported as "not UTF-8" (None) even though it is valid UTF-8. The new `limit=None` path does not have this flaw. The capped path is still used by `build()` (whether a source file is delivered) and by `withheld_text` (signoff.py:753 and :758).
scenario: a builder-notes file larger than 512 KiB with a "€" or "é" at byte 524289. `entry_text_or_none` returns None, so the notes add nothing to `withheld_text`. A reviewer quoting those notes is then not refused on independence; the refusal fails open. Separately, a large source file with the same layout is listed "binary or not UTF-8 text" and never delivered, so the reviewer never sees it.

claim: `withheld_text` reads the ledger document through the capped reader. For a ledger doc over 512 KiB, any withheld section or `Status:` line past the cap is missing from `withheld_text`. A quotation of it is therefore not refused.
scenario: a plan doc of 600 KiB whose `## Deviations` section sits past 512 KiB. A reviewer quoting a Deviations sentence passes the quoted-span check, because `needle in withheld` is False.

claim: `adjudicate` has a second independence gate, `answer.py` `citations(row, withheld_lines)`, called at answer.py:567, 571 and 578. That gate refuses any answer text containing a withheld line of 24 characters or more, and it never consults `delivered_text`. A sentence that appears both in the builder's notes and in a delivered file is refused whenever the reviewer quotes the whole line. Packet size makes no difference. Requirement 1 says "a quotation that appears anywhere in the delivered packet traces to it", which holds only for the `provenance_citations` path.
scenario: the builder's notes contain the line "The late separator sentence held in every run." and a delivered file carries the same line. The reviewer writes notes `The packet closes with "The late separator sentence held in every run." at its very end.` `record-answer` then exits 10 with `refusal_reason: independence`, `why: "the verdict quotes the builder's own account of its work"`. The same refusal happens unquoted, and on a small packet with no file near the cap. So a live run like Slice D's can still stop on independence over delivered words, depending on how the reviewer quotes.

claim: the helper strips the trailing period before quoting. The normalized withheld line `...every run.` is then not a substring of the answer, so `citations()` never fires and only `provenance_citations` is tested. With the period kept, `ALateQuotationTracesToTheDeliveredText` would fail with an independence refusal.
scenario: a later change breaks or narrows the delivered-text exemption on the line-check path, and this suite stays green. The test proves less than its name says.

claim: the material is roughly the number of files times up to 512 KiB, plus headers. A large source set (for example thousands of files) produces a material of hundreds of MB. `record-answer` reads all of it into memory, then `_normalize` builds a second lowercased, re-joined copy and runs a substring search per quoted span. Before this change the read stopped at 512 KiB.
scenario: a slice touching a vendored tree with many large files. `record-answer` slows down or runs out of memory. A traceback is not JSON on stdout.
